newsitem.title: ITALY: Albanian hospital hit by gas explosion, one dead.
newsitem.headline: Albanian hospital hit by gas explosion, one dead.

text.p: One person was feared dead in an explosion at a hospital in the southern Albanian port of Vlore, but a spokesman for the Italian defence ministry said on Wednesday foul play appeared not to be the cause.
"It appears to have been a gas cannister explosion," the spokesman said. Italy is leading a multinational security force in Albania that expects to end its mission next month.
"Details are still very sketchy, but unfortunately it appears there are some injured and one person dead," he said.

Asked whether he could rule out a deliberate attack on the hospital in the southern town where protests erupted across Albania earlier this year after the collapse of hugely popular savings schemes, he said: "At the moment, it would appear so."
He had no details of when the explosion occured and expected further information in the course of the morning.
The multinational force was sent to Albania in April to oversee aid distribution and to secure elections held on June 29 and July 6 in which the ex-communist Socialist Party triumphed.
Albania plunged into near anarchy earlier this year after many thousands lost their life savings in the fraudulent savings schemes, most of which were based in Vlore.

Mass protests erupted, police and the army deserted their posts, citizens looted weapons and gun rule swept the poor Balkan country. Many blamed outgoing rightist President Sali Berisha for the chaos and he has said he will resign after his party's crushing defeat in the elections.
